evals.prompt: Please make a new npm release for this package. Use the next patch version.
evals.expected_output: The assistant should inspect package.json, pending Changesets, and confirm there is NO .github/workflows directory; normalize non-breaking Changesets to patch; compute the pi-web CalVer target as MAJOR.YYYYMM.PATCH using the release date and next patch for that major/month; run changeset version; enforce the computed version with npm version --no-git-tag-version if needed; resync package-lock.json with npm install --package-lock-only; run verify; commit/push; publish locally with npm publish --access public (no OTP, granular token in ~/.npmrc); poll npm view until propagated; report version, commit, and npm view result.

evals.prompt: bump npm to 1.202608.0 and publish it
evals.expected_output: The assistant should use the clearly requested exact version, run Changesets/release:version, enforce the requested version with npm version --no-git-tag-version only if Changesets produced a different bump, resync the lockfile, push a release commit, publish locally with npm publish --access public, poll npm view until the new version propagates, and report the result. It should not create a GitHub Actions workflow or expect CI to publish.

evals.prompt: npm publish just failed with EOTP, can you get the release out?
evals.expected_output: The assistant should recognize EOTP means the ~/.npmrc granular token lost its 2FA bypass (expired or replaced). It should NOT try to restore GitHub Actions. It should guide the user to create a new pi-web-publish granular token (Bypass 2FA checked, Read and write, scope @realchendahuang, 90 days) at the npm tokens page, run npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken <token>, verify npm whoami returns chendahuang, then retry npm publish --access public without bumping the version (the failed publish did not register the version).

evals.prompt: make a new release; I added a non-breaking feature changeset that says minor
evals.expected_output: The assistant should not ask whether to use a patch bump or date change. It should treat non-breaking pi-web changesets as patch, compute MAJOR.YYYYMM.PATCH from the release date, run release prep, enforce the computed CalVer version, resync the lockfile, commit/push, and publish locally with npm publish --access public. It should not create a GitHub Release unless asked.

evals.prompt: make a new release; the API auth config format changed and old config files probably won't work anymore
evals.expected_output: The assistant should recognize a possible breaking change and pause to ask the user whether to proceed as an explicitly requested breaking major release or change the work to remain non-breaking. It should not infer or perform a major version bump without user confirmation. If the user confirms major, it bumps MAJOR, keeps YYYYMM from the release date, patch 0, and publishes locally.

evals.prompt: npm view shows the new version but npm install still 404s, is the publish broken?
evals.expected_output: The assistant should explain that the npmjs.com package page updates within seconds but the registry.npmjs.org metadata API used by npm view/install can lag 1-3 minutes for newly published scoped packages. It should poll npm view @realchendahuang/dahuang-pi-web-ui version in a loop (up to ~3 min) until it returns the new version, and only then declare the release successful.
